ruling.recommended_action: Close as no_action: record the RD-1 breach finding (unexempted 2.36 km off-route segment, F3) on the driver's file; no refund is due because the RydeX fare is a fixed quote unaffected by mileage.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a fixed-quote RydeX booking: $34.32 charged, broken into base $3.90, distance $23.31 (16.53 km), time $5.64 (21.7 min), waiting $0.00 and platform $1.47 [F6], with no surge (1.0×) [F5] and a billed distance of 16.5 km that does not exceed the optimal route [F4]. Under RD-2's non-metered branch, the fare is a quote set at booking and does not vary with mileage, so the refundable amount from any detour is $0.00; the RD-2 formula therefore yields 2.36 km × $0 = $0.00 [F3][F4][F6][RD-2]. A refundable amount of 0 gives no_action, with the driver's breach of the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty recorded [RD-2].

The GPS record shows exactly one off-route segment: 09:07–09:14, 4.13 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.77 km, +2.36 km and up to 1304 m from the optimal route, against a whole-trip actual of 19.1 km vs 16.5 km optimal (+2.6 km, +16%) and +7.4 min duration [F1][F2][F3]. That segment is a deviation requiring justification under RD-1, and none of RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 excuses it, so it counts [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 does not exempt it. No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F13], and the only traffic facts are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the AYE and CTE during 08:42–09:26 [F11][F12]; band 4 is outside the band 1–2 range RD-4(b) contemplates, so at most it is corroboration and cannot by itself exempt a segment, and with no qualifying incident there is no RD-4(a) excuse [RD-4].

RD-5 does not exempt it either. The chat is complete and every message is timestamped [F9], and its only contents are the rider's 08:48 pickup message ("I'm at the Victoria Street entrance already, in a grey hoodie") and the driver's 08:48 reply about the car [F7][F8]. There is therefore no rider message sent before the segment began at 09:07 agreeing to any route change; the driver's post-trip statement "I followed my GPS; it rerouted me" is not consent and, per RD-5, a driver's claim of agreement cannot establish consent [F10][RD-5]. A complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment means the segment counts [RD-5].

RD-3 does not apply: no stop was measured in this segment and the rider never named any intermediate place — the only rider message is about the pickup point [F7][F3][RD-3]. RD-6 is not triggered: the driver has 0 upheld disputes and 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so the "repeated breach" predicate for flag_account is absent [F16][RD-6].

On the fare, no unpublished or non-qualifying charge appears: the components in [F6] are all published items (base, distance, time, waiting, platform), there is no toll/ERP line and no post-trip add-on, so FARE-1 requires no refund [F6][FARE-1]. The complaint seeks no money and asks only that the deviation be recorded, which is precisely what RD-2's zero-amount branch produces [F4][F6][RD-2].

Safety screen: I read the two chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint — they concern pickup arrangements, the route taken and the fare, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern is "none" [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence status is sufficient: the GPS records measure the segment and the fare, and the chat is complete and timestamped, so every element this ruling needs is settled [F3][F6][F9].

segment_findings.reason: The 09:07–09:14 off-route segment (4.13 km driven vs 1.77 km optimal, +2.36 km, up to 1304 m off route) is unexempted. The chat is complete and timestamped and contains only two 08:48 pickup messages, so there is no rider message sent before 09:07 agreeing to any route change [F7][F8][F9]; the driver's post-trip statement that his GPS rerouted him is not consent and cannot excuse the segment [F10][RD-5]. No incident supports an RD-4(a) excuse and the band-4 speed facts do not qualify under RD-4(b) [F13][F11][F12][RD-4], and no rider-named stop exists in this segment [F7][RD-3]. The segment therefore counts under RD-1/RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: True but not exonerating: the fixed RydeX quote [F6] means the extra 2.36 km [F3] cost the rider nothing, which is why the RD-2 amount is $0.00 — but that does not answer the RD-1 shortest-and-most-direct-route duty, which on [F3] was breached.

Accepted only as to amount: on a non-metered RydeX trip the RD-2 refund for the F3 segment is $0.00 [F4][F6][RD-2]. RD-2 still records the driver's RD-1 breach, so the claim that the segment's only consequence is nothing does not stand.

Rejected: [F11] and [F12] are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h), outside the band 1–2 RD-4(b) contemplates, and [F13] records no incident, so the reroute is not excused by RD-4 and the segment counts under RD-2 [F11][F12][F13][RD-4].

Rejected: arrival at the rider's named destination [F2][F3] does not exempt the 1304 m excursion; RD-5 requires the rider's own message before the segment agreeing to the route, and the complete chat [F7][F8][F9] contains none [RD-5].

Accepted as to the $0.00 RD-2 amount for this fixed-fare trip [F4][F5][F6][RD-2], but the requested no_action plus recorded breach is granted on the reasoning above; nothing in this claim would support a monetary refund.
